questionText:
An array $A$ of length $n$ with distinct elements is said to be bitonic if there is an index $1 \le i \le n$ such that $A[1\dots i]$ is sorted in the non-decreasing order and $A[i + 1\dots n]$ is sorted in the non-increasing order.

Which ONE of the following represents the best possible asymptotic bound for the worst-case number of comparisons by an algorithm that searches for an element in a bitonic array $A$?
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

Searching an element in a bitonic array can be efficiently performed in three binary search phases:

1. Find the Bitonic Point (Peak Element):
• Use a binary search variant to find the peak element index $i$ where $A[i]$ is maximum.
• Comparing $A[mid]$ with its neighbors determines whether to move left or right.
• Number of comparisons: $O(\log n)$.

2. Binary Search in the Left Subarray:
• The prefix $A[1\dots i]$ is sorted in increasing order.
• Perform a standard binary search on this subarray.
• Number of comparisons: $O(\log n)$.

3. Binary Search in the Right Subarray:
• The suffix $A[i+1\dots n]$ is sorted in decreasing order.
• If the element is not found in the left subarray, perform a reverse binary search on this subarray.
• Number of comparisons: $O(\log n)$.

Total Worst-case Comparisons:
$$T(n) = O(\log n) + O(\log n) + O(\log n) = \Theta(\log n)$$

Hence, Option (D) is correct.
